blockMcqs.question: What is the real goal when training an ML model?
options: Memorize the training examples perfectly
Generalize to data it has never seen
Hand-code the rules more precisely
Minimize the number of features used
blockMcqs.explanation: Memorizing examples is easy and useless; performing on unseen inputs is the point.

blockMcqs.question: Which paradigm learns from labeled input-to-answer pairs?
options: Unsupervised learning
Reinforcement learning
Supervised learning
Dimensionality reduction
blockMcqs.explanation: Labels give the clearest signal, which is why supervised dominates industry ML.

blockMcqs.question: What does the learning rate control in gradient descent?
options: How wrong each prediction is
The size of each parameter step
The number of features used
How data is split into folds
blockMcqs.explanation: Too large a step overshoots the minimum; too small makes training crawl.

blockMcqs.question: Why keep a test set separate from the validation set?
options: Validation data is always too small
Tuning choices leak info and inflate validation
The test set trains the final model
Test data uses a different loss function
blockMcqs.explanation: Each choice made on validation contaminates it, so the locked test set gives an honest number.

blockMcqs.question: A model scores high on training but poorly on new data. This is:
options: Underfitting (high bias)
Overfitting (high variance)
Irreducible noise
A serving skew bug
blockMcqs.explanation: It memorized training noise, so the large train-vs-test gap signals high variance.

blockMcqs.question: With 99% legit and 1% fraud, why is accuracy misleading?
options: Accuracy can't be computed on imbalanced data
Always predicting legit scores 99% yet catches no fraud
Precision and recall are undefined here
The test set becomes contaminated
blockMcqs.explanation: A useless majority-class predictor looks great, so you need precision, recall, F1, or AUC.

blockMcqs.question: A bank must explain every loan rejection. This favors:
options: A deep neural network for max accuracy
An interpretable model like logistic regression
A large tree ensemble for robustness
Unsupervised clustering of applicants
blockMcqs.explanation: Regulation makes interpretability outweigh the small accuracy gain of opaque models.

blockMcqs.question: What problem does a feature store solve?
options: It speeds up gradient descent during training
It serves identical features to training and inference
It automatically labels raw data
It removes the need for a validation set
blockMcqs.explanation: Consistent features prevent training/serving skew, where prod features differ from training.
